chapter_title: Designing an A/B Test with Students
learning_objective: The learner will critique the eight sections of a draft test plan, deciding for each whether it is sound or flawed, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** test-plan-reviewer
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Evaluate
**Bloom Verb:** critique
**Learning Objective:** The learner will critique the eight sections of a draft test plan, deciding for each whether it is sound or flawed, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Test Hypothesis, Control Group, Treatment Group, Random Assignment, Outcome Measure, Sample Size, Confounding Variable, Informed Consent, Student Privacy in Testing (all defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each section the learner commits Sound or Flawed. A verdict is correct when it matches the Correct verdict column in Content. When the verdict is Flawed, the learner also names the flaw from the list, and the name is checked in the feedback. Mastery is at least 7 of 8 verdicts correct on the first attempt. Reading the chapter summary is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) A plan is sound if it has all the section headings. (2) A small test can prove that a version works. (3) A note sent home after the test counts as consent. **Instructional Rationale:** Critiquing a plan section by section is an Evaluate-level action that brings the chapter's concepts together. Four flawed and four sound sections teach the learner to find the weak point and to leave a sound section alone. **Content:** The two verdicts: Sound, Flawed. The flaws: Vague hypothesis, Confounded groups, Overclaim from a small sample, Consent after the test, Privacy gap. The eight sections of the draft plan (all made up, for a Watershed Basics pilot): | # | Section | Text of the draft | Correct verdict | Flaw | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Hypothesis | The improved version will be better. | Flawed | Vague hypothesis | "Better" has no measure, size, or direction. | | 2 | Groups | The control group is the third-period class using the original. The treatment group is the fifth-period class using the improved version. | Flawed | Confounded groups | The periods differ in students, time of day, and more. | | 3 | Assignment | Students are paired by pre-test score, and a random number decides which student in each pair gets the improved version. | Sound | None | It is blocked random assignment. | | 4 | Outcome measure | Both groups take a 20-question test written for the three learning outcomes, with the same key, before and after the lesson. | Sound | None | The measure is aligned, the same for both, and scored alike. | | 5 | Sample size and claim | All 24 students in one class take part, and the result will be reported as proof that the improved version works for all Grade 6 students. | Flawed | Overclaim from a small sample | A pilot of 24 students cannot prove an effect for all students. | | 6 | Consent | Students take part as a class activity, and a note will be sent home afterward. | Flawed | Consent after the test | Consent must come before any data is collected. | | 7 | Privacy | Scores are stored under code numbers, the key is kept in a separate locked file, and no names are sent to any AI agent. | Sound | None | It follows the minimization, code, and agent practices. | | 8 | Timeline | The pre-test is in week 1, the lesson is in weeks 2 and 3, and the post-test is in week 4, on the same days for both groups. | Sound | None | The conditions are the same for both groups. | **Provenance:** The sections are illustrative examples written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The flaws follow the chapter sections on the hypothesis, the groups, the sample, consent, and privacy. **Rules:** Each section has exactly one correct verdict. Four are Flawed and four are Sound. The flaw named for each Flawed section is unique. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one section of the plan. 2. The learner chooses Sound or Flawed. If Flawed, the learner also names the flaw. 3. The sim shows whether the verdict was correct, the flaw, and the Why text. 4. After section 8 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 8 sections in the order of the table, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [verdict]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. This section is [verdict]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 8 correct on the first attempt". At 7 or more it adds "You can review a test plan." Below 7 it lists the Why text of each missed section. **Starting State:** Section 1 of the draft plan and the two verdicts. The question shown is "Is this section ready to use?" **Chapter Anchors:** The sections correspond to the chapter's hypothesis, groups, assignment, outcome measure, sample size, consent, privacy, and the timeline of the eight-step method.
